lines.assertion: Calendar-year 2026, BYN. Individuals resident under General Code art. 17 are taxed on Belarus and foreign-source income; nonresidents on Belarus-source income (Special Code arts. 195-198). Residence means more than 183 days in Belarus, with the statutory temporary-absence rules, prior-year provisional status and treaty tie-breaker. Count from the day after arrival through departure. Citizenship or a residence permit alone does not replace that test; art. 17(5) supplies a fallback where no applicable treaty resolves residence. [General Code art. 17](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0200166); [Special Code arts. 195-198](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

Before calculating business tax, classify the activity and legal status. From 2026 continuing entrepreneurs must be on the permitted activity list under Council Resolution 457 of 28 June 2024. Professional income is a separate regime for permitted independent professional activities, using the app, rather than an entrepreneur turnover election. Employment income and civil-contract work/service receipts from a current employer, or a former employer that employed the person less than three years ago, are outside that regime (art. 379). The single tax is available only within arts. 335-337; short-stay accommodation by entrepreneurs must use it under art. 336(5). [MNS activity transition](https://nalog.gov.by/news/33527/); [Code arts. 335-337, 378-380](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

**Ordinary individuals.** Classify each receipt under arts. 196-203; value in-kind benefits under art. 200. Exclude only a verified art. 208 exemption. Common nonbusiness disposals are exempt under art. 208(44): one of each listed real-estate type in five years and one eligible vehicle per calendar year, with the citizenship/nonresident extension and business-asset exclusions in that paragraph. For an eligible taxable disposal under art. 211(1.2), deduct qualifying evidenced acquisition/disposal costs or the 20% alternative, never both. BYN costs are converted to USD at the National Bank rate on the cost date and back to BYN at the income-receipt-date rate; do not make that conversion if the cost-date BYN/USD rate is higher than the receipt-date rate (retain nominal BYN costs in that case). Costs originally paid in foreign currency are converted at the relevant income-receipt-date rate. Allocate co-owned costs by ownership share and acquisition costs proportionately to instalment proceeds. In nonresident cases assessed under art. 218, paragraph 5 expressly grants the art. 211(1.2) deduction for immovable-property income; do not automatically extend that route to movable-property receipts without checking their own source/agent/classification rules. Securities, company interests and intellectual property need their own classification; do not extend the ordinary personal-property exemption to them. [Arts. 196-203, 208(44), 211(1.2)](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

Apply art. 209 standard deductions at the main employment/study place. Without one, obtain the written election and supporting documents; only one agent or the tax authority supplies the relevant standard deductions. Entrepreneurs without a main job apply them only for the qualifying months and test the statutory quarterly income limit. Do not multiply the monthly income limit to invent that quarterly figure. Unused standard deductions do not create a negative tax base (art. 199(3)). [Arts. 199(3), 209(2)](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

Art. 210 allows evidenced qualifying Belarus first higher, secondary-specialist or vocational education costs and qualifying Belarus voluntary insurance, including eligible family expenditure. Qualifying life/additional-pension insurance requires a term of at least three years. Art. 211(1.1) allows evidenced qualifying Belarus home construction/acquisition and related loan repayments for persons registered as needing better housing. Keep the eligibility and payment documents listed in arts. 210-211; carry unused qualifying social/housing deductions forward under those articles, without also deducting a reimbursement. The young-specialist deduction requires the specified placement/service documents and employment continuity conditions in art. 209(1.4); age alone is insufficient. [Arts. 209-211](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

**High income.** Aggregate only the Belarus-source items listed in art. 199(8-2), including employment, taxable employer compensation, civil-contract work/services/IP, loan interest to agents, rent and board fees; exclude the paragraph's stated items. Dividends form the separate art. 199(8-3) base. Apply ordinary taxation below the thresholds, then assess the excess at the higher rates and credit tax already imposed on that excess under art. 219(1.9). Do not assess the higher tax again on the first band or pool dividends with wages. Deductions/exemptions in arts. 208-212 cannot reduce the excess above the high-income threshold. Foreign income is not automatically part of this specified Belarus-source pool. [Arts. 199(8-2)-(8-3), 214, 219(1.9)](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

**Entrepreneurs.** Assemble business revenue and other business income under art. 205 and receipt dates under art. 213, including statutory treatment of advances, barter, third-party payments and discontinued-business receipts. Choose evidenced business costs or the deemed-cost election, documented in writing for the year. Do not combine the two. Actual expenses follow art. 205: match stock, depreciate qualifying capital assets, exclude private costs, capital acquisition costs already recovered by depreciation, tax penalties and costs of exempt/special-regime income. Expenses cannot generally exceed period income; art. 205(11) specifically carries qualifying registration, bank-opening, rent/utilities and licensing excess costs until used. Do not apply corporate loss rules. Calculate the cumulative base, allowable personal deductions, the whole-year rate and subtract earlier instalments. [Arts. 199, 205, 213-214, 217](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

**Professional income.** First test the art. 379 object: Belarus citizens can include Belarus-source and foreign-source professional income; other eligible taxpayers can include Belarus-source professional income and the specified Belarus-located property income, with foreign-source professional receipts outside this object. A foreign customer alone does not settle income source. Exclude current-employer and less-than-three-years former-employer civil-contract work/service receipts. Art. 379 also excludes separately charged tenant utility/service reimbursements where the contract requires reimbursement outside rent, and buyer delivery reimbursements outside the goods price. Then tax eligible receipts without business-expense deductions, tracking Belarus business-customer income separately from individuals and foreign customers. Form app receipts for each settlement; refund/correction rules are in art. 381-1. The pension exemption removes the social-insurance component, leaving 4%/8% effective rates, rather than an across-the-board 8%. From July compare the monthly result with the applicable minimum even in a zero-receipt month while registered. The former first-user BYN 2,000 deduction ended on 1 January 2026. [Arts. 381-1 through 381-7](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071); [FSZN Law art. 16-1](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=H12100118); [MNS 2026 changes](https://nalog.gov.by/clarifications/comments/33519/).

The new schedule applies where the statutory payment deadline falls after 30 January; January continuing activities retain the former schedule, while newly eligible construction/taxi use the new one. January-only eligible retail for fewer than 15 days at a trading place, exhibition/sale, fair or itinerant/peddling trade uses coefficient 0.5. It does not continue from February. Initial construction/taxi elections from January require the Q1 return by 31 January and January payment by 1 February, subject to General Code art. 4 nonworking-day adjustment. [127-Z art. 4(5)](https://pravo.by/upload/docs/op/H12500127_1767214800.pdf); [MNS transition](https://nalog.gov.by/clarifications/clarifications/33616/).

For each month, charge each trading object/place separately, subject to art. 342(5)'s precise no-other-persons trading-place/itinerant exception. Use the highest product rate for mixed retail. Several other services use the highest service rate, but add a separate charge for each short-stay property. Taxi uses tax-registration location; other activities use activity location. Keep shipment/performance revenue and other income under art. 342(15)-(25); unassigned mixed-regime other income follows the revenue-share allocation. [Art. 342(1)-(25)](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

Art. 340 reduces tax 25% for the first three months beginning with first business activity; 20% for qualifying pension, disability, three-or-more minor children or disabled-child grounds; multiple simultaneous grounds within (1.1)-(1.5) give a total 45% reduction. The specified group I/II disabled-parent and spouse conditions in (1.6) give 100%. Obtain the exact status documents and apply the statutory month boundaries. Entrepreneurs choose one object/place/activity for relief, not every unit. Ordinary individuals' relief rules differ and exclude their short-stay activity. Sum the fixed charges after eligible relief; surcharge is `6% × max(0, quarter revenue − 40 × quarter fixed tax BEFORE relief)`. Supported art. 344 absence grounds require application/evidence for proration, `monthly charge × active days / calendar days`; there is no unrestricted part-month election. [Arts. 340, 342(14),(30), 344](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

**Rent.** Multiply the monthly rate by taxable units and prorate first/last partial months by days under art. 221(2). Under art. 221(3), a 10% supplementary assessment applies to stated rental income exceeding ten times fixed PIT paid for the relevant period when that income is given in the specified income/expenditure-check explanations. It is not an automatic annual rent surtax. Renting to a business is outside the private fixed-rent rule. [Arts. 214(2), 221](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

Use the tax inspectorate or MNS personal cabinet for individual declarations; entrepreneur electronic filing follows General Code art. 40. Apply General Code art. 4 to nonworking-day tax deadlines, rather than assuming contribution payment dates follow the same convention. [General Code arts. 4, 28, 40](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0200166).

Late-payment interest under General Tax Code art. 55 is computed separately for each period of constant unpaid tax and National Bank refinancing rate: `unpaid tax × overdue calendar days × annual rate / 360 / 100`. Count from the day after the due date through payment; interest reflected in the audit decision on audit-assessed tax is capped at that assessed tax amount; apply art. 55(3) exclusions and art. 55(4)'s four-decimal interest-rate precision. Use the rate actually in force in each period, not a single assumed 2026 rate. [General Code art. 55](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0200166).

For an ordinary individual with tax payable and a return more than 30 working days late, Administrative Code art. 14.2(3) sets 0.5 basic unit plus 0.5 per complete month, capped at 10. Negligent ordinary-individual underpayment above one basic unit carries 15%, minimum 0.5 basic unit under art. 14.4(6); intentional cases use art. 14.4(8), 40%, minimum 10 basic units. Apply the statutory exclusions and correction rules before estimating a fine. For a business/agent return, Administrative Code art. 14.2(1)-(2) sets up to 1 basic unit for no more than 3 working days late; otherwise 2 basic units plus 0.5 per complete month, capped at 10. Repetition within a year invokes art. 14.2(4), 3 per complete or incomplete month, capped at 20. Under art. 14.4(1), business tax underpayment carries 40% of unpaid tax, minimum 2 basic units for an entrepreneur or 10 for a company, subject to the statutory notes, including timely voluntary correction/payment. Do not apply these amounts automatically to an ordinary individual or to a withholding default. [Administrative Code arts. 14.2 and 14.4](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk2100091).

Unregistered prohibited business income and the other specified art. 214(7) cases use 26%, distinct from an administrative fine. Unreceipted/late-receipted professional income uses 20% without the pension relief (art. 381-2(2)); from July repeated nonpayment three times triggers authority deregistration and the art. 381(4) re-entry rule. [Arts. 214(7), 381, 381-2](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

Convert foreign receipts at the National Bank rate on actual receipt, with the specific monthly employment and entrepreneur-advance rules in art. 199(11). Resident foreign-tax credits are calculated income by income, limited to Belarus tax on that income, with the art. 224 evidence and offshore exception; entrepreneur credits use art. 224(3). Read `belarus-cross-border-tax` before applying a treaty. [Arts. 199(11), 224](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

Nonresident art. 218 cases require a declaration of expected Belarus income before the activity/disposal/rental starts and advance payment, with real-estate tax payable within five working days after notice; actual-income reconciliation and additional payment also have five-working-day rules. Belarus citizens departing permanently must file and pay the art. 222(5) departure assessment, within 15 calendar days of notice and no later than departure. Agent withholding alone does not remove the annual high-income declaration obligation. [Arts. 214(1.2)-(1.3), 218, 222(5)](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

Calendar-year 2026 ordinary Belarus organisations, separately liable branches under General Code art. 14 and foreign organisations operating through a Belarus PE. Identify the taxpayer and separate regime before consolidating any figures; the increased-rate test is applied separately to the organisation excluding branches, each branch and each foreign PE (art. 184(1)). Resident organisations' gross profit includes foreign activity; foreign PEs compute attributable Belarus profit under art. 180. [General Code arts. 14-16](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0200166); [Special Code arts. 166-167, 180, 184](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

Screen the simplified system before ordinary profit tax: only eligible organisations under arts. 324-327 qualify. Entrepreneurs cannot use this company regime. Do not apply ordinary profit tax to receipts replaced by the simplified tax, or treat the replacement as removing dividend, withholding or import/reverse-charge VAT obligations. [Arts. 324-326](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

1. Start with revenue from sales less taxes from revenue and allowable production/selling costs, plus taxable non-operating income less allowable non-operating expenses. Reconcile separately disposed depreciable assets, investment property and intangible assets using proceeds less residual value and sale costs under art. 168. Do not treat all accounting income/expenses as taxable/deductible. [Arts. 167-175](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

2. Recognise revenue and costs at the statutory dates, document business purpose and matching, and depreciate qualifying capital expenditure. Add back art. 173 nondeductible costs, including tax sanctions and private expenditure. Apply art. 171(1)'s separate limits to travel, fuel, management and the other listed controlled costs. Pool the art. 171(2) other costs, including listed employee retirement/health payments, representation, board fees, official events, non-travelling staff's private-car compensation, association fees, late-loan interest, promotional gifts and employee transport. Their combined deduction is at most 1% of revenue from goods/work/services/IP and other assets, INCLUDING VAT, under art. 171(3); test the exact listed inclusions/exceptions before pooling. [Arts. 168-175](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

3. Apply the investment deduction only to qualifying assets and reconstruction, within the statutory ceiling and two-year claim window beginning with the reporting period containing the qualifying depreciation or reconstruction-capitalisation month. Ordinary passenger cars are excluded unless within the specified special-purpose, taxi or carsharing categories. Test the other excluded assets and recapture on disqualifying disposal/use changes under art. 170(2.2). For the 2026 reform, depreciation must start from 1 January 2026 or reconstruction must increase original cost after that date; do not retroactively apply the expanded timing to older assets. An investment deduction not claimed before an appointed inspection is unavailable for the inspected period. [Art. 170(2.2)](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071); [MNS reform commentary](https://nalog.gov.by/clarifications/comments/33570/).

4. Calculate controlled indebtedness at year end across the counterparties in art. 172(2.1), including qualifying related-party borrowings and specified service/IP/penalty obligations. Equity excludes the statutory tax, contribution and budget-loan liabilities. For an ordinary company with positive equity, `capitalisation coefficient = controlled debt / equity / 3`; if the trigger applies, divide the affected otherwise deductible costs and interest by that coefficient. With nonpositive equity, none of those affected costs is deductible. Excisable producers use the alternative coefficient; banking, insurance and qualifying majority-rental businesses have art. 172(4) exclusions. This is a cost cap, separate from arm's-length TP. [Art. 172](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

5. Separate exempt profit, dividends and special-rate bases. Apply TP adjustments under General Code arts. 87-97. Compute the cumulative ordinary rate from the statutory tax base, not revenue, accounting profit or only the excess above the increased-rate threshold. [Arts. 182, 184, 186](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071); [General Code ch. 11](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0200166).

6. Claim carried losses only in the final annual/fourth-quarter computation under art. 186(1). Maintain losses by vintage, expiry, taxpayer and statutory basket. Securities/financial-instrument losses and fixed/investment-asset disposal losses are generally usable against their corresponding basket; residual losses follow art. 183(3.2). Use oldest eligible losses first, within current qualifying profit. Exclude foreign separately registered activity, exempt/regime-period losses and undocumented losses as art. 183 requires. A loss not claimed before an appointed non-desk inspection cannot be introduced during that inspection. Do not carry a subsidiary's loss to another company or assume all reorganisations transfer it. [Art. 183](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

7. Multiply each remaining rate-specific base by its rate; subtract allowable art. 187 foreign-tax credit and earlier cumulative tax payments. Corporate foreign credit is capped at Belarus tax on the corresponding qualifying foreign income. Preserve foreign authority/payment evidence and the timing/translation rules of art. 187, rather than subtracting all overseas cash tax. [Arts. 186-187](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

**Simplified route.** Screen all art. 324 exclusions, including regulated activities, prohibited property use/subletting, and ownership/entity categories. Test employee and revenue limits separately. For existing 2025 users, revenue above BYN 3,500,000 in 2025 blocks continuation in 2026 despite the higher 2026 limit. An eligible newly registered company with no more than 50 employees can notify within 20 working days; ordinary next-year entry notification is 1 October-31 December. Exit is from the month after the reporting period of an employee/revenue excess, or from the relevant disqualifying month under art. 327(6.1). 1. **Classify the supply and place.** Domestic taxable turnover and imports are within art. 115, subject to exclusions. Goods use art. 116, including where located or dispatched. For services, art. 117 takes priority by category: immovable-property location, physical movable-property work, specified actually performed services, customer location for listed consultancy/accounting/legal/advertising/IP and similar services, then the residual supplier-location rule. Do not apply a single B2B customer-location rule to every service. EAEU transactions require the applicable treaty/indirect-tax protocol as well. [Arts. 115-117](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

2. **Separate taxable, exempt and zero-rated turnover.** Art. 118 exemptions, including qualifying health, education and financial services, have their own conditions. Zero rating requires the evidence and deadlines in arts. 123-126; a foreign customer is not proof of zero rating. Keep export goods, transport and other services distinct. [Arts. 118, 122-126](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

3. **Set the base and tax point.** Ordinarily base equals consideration including excise but excluding VAT (art. 120). Include statutory price supplements, contractual sanctions and relevant noncash/free transfers under arts. 115/120. Use shipment/performance and the specific timing rules of art. 121, not an assumed receipt rule for all domestic supplies. For tax-exclusive value, output VAT is base times rate; for tax-inclusive value, VAT is gross times rate divided by one plus rate. Track returns, cancellations, price changes and currency conversion under arts. 120-121/129-130 and issue corrected/additional invoices under art. 131. [Arts. 120-121, 128-131](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

4. **Purchaser tax-agent VAT.** Where a foreign supplier is not registered and the supply is located in Belarus, the Belarus purchaser fulfils the obligation under art. 114 even when not an ordinary domestic VAT payer. Determine the base/rate and tax point under the applicable statutory provisions and create the purchaser electronic invoice. Claim purchaser input VAT only when the art. 132-133 payment, accounting and document conditions are met; no automatic immediate offset. [Arts. 114, 120-122, 129, 131-133](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

5. **Establish credits.** Domestic input tax requires a seller invoice received and signed with the purchaser's electronic signature, accounted acquisition and, if elected, entry in the purchase book. Import tax requires payment and the customs or EAEU return/payment documents plus the portal invoice. Purchaser-agent tax requires the return and portal invoice and statutory payment conditions. An ordinary unpaid domestic supplier invoice is not disallowed solely because unpaid, subject to exceptions. Do not claim undocumented or exempt-use input tax. [Art. 132(1),(3)-(5)](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

6. **Allocate mixed credits.** Use the accounting-policy separate-accounting or turnover-share method consistently through the calendar year; turnover share is default if no policy specifies the method. Under art. 134(3), the denominator and relevant turnover are VAT-inclusive, including statutory base adjustments. Allocate exempt-use ordinary input tax to costs under art. 133(3), distinguish capital/intangible credits, and apply art. 135's ordering and output-tax limits. Retain unutilised limited credits. Special eligible zero/reduced-rate credits are deductible beyond output tax under arts. 133(27)/135(2); do not call every excess a refundable cash balance. [Arts. 133-135](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

Follow art. 137 for eligible excess-credit set-off/refund: apply to the inspectorate, reconcile arrears and retain the supporting documents. Under art. 137(2), with the VAT return on file, the decision is due within two working days of the written application, electronic acceptance confirmation or completion of the applicable check, and is sent within five working days. An ordinary verification inspection under art. 137(3) is appointed within two working days and the verification period is no more than fifteen working days from the refund application; liquidation and exported-oil-product cases have distinct timing. The ordinary set-off period is thirty calendar days after the decision; the remaining eligible balance is refunded within five working days after that period, subject to budget/tax debts. Art. 137(5-1) delays payment for an evidence notice or later inspection: apply its ten-working-day period after accepted evidence/desk-audit act, or five working days after the later inspection act, and never earlier than the ordinary refund deadline. **Control screen.** Classify related foreign trade; domestic transactions with a related Belarus legal entity entitled to profit-tax nonpayment/exemption; the specific property/share/loan category; and strategic-goods foreign trade. The 2026 art. 88(1.3) category expressly includes the listed zone/preferential-regime counterparties and foreign related transactions. Aggregate sales and purchases separately per counterparty for the calendar year, excluding VAT/excise. For loans, transaction price for threshold purposes is principal; include annual new advances/tranches plus the opening outstanding balance where the year's loan transaction occurs. This is not the interest-income base, and an unchanged historical loan is not automatically a new annual advance. [Art. 88(4)](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0200166); [MNS loan clarification](https://nalog.gov.by/organizations/transfer_pricing/questions/).

**Comparability.** Record contract and actual conduct, product/service/IP features, functions, assets, risks, market/economic conditions and business strategy under art. 89. Adjust material differences with evidence. Use official/public market sources or documented third-party data under art. 90, not a made-up markup. For loans examine currency, term/tranche, security, credit quality, interest type and repayment. [Arts. 89-90, 92](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0200166).

**Methods and calculation.** Art. 91 prefers the comparable uncontrolled price (CUP) method where it and another method can be used. Otherwise select the most reliable supported resale-price, cost-plus, comparable-profitability or profit-split method; combining methods is permitted. A less complex tested party with fewer risks and no valuable influencing intangibles is the preferred profitability tested party under art. 91(5). [Arts. 91-96](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0200166).

- CUP compares adjusted comparable prices with the controlled price. A single comparable can set both bounds only if conditions are comparable/adjustable and the comparable seller is not dominant (art. 92(6)).

- Resale price compares gross margin on resale to an independent buyer; cost-plus compares gross profit/cost. Use the art. 91 financial definitions consistently, without mixing gross and operating margins (arts. 93-94).

- Comparable profitability uses the supported operating profit/sales, costs, assets or other permitted indicator under arts. 91(8), 95. For an out-of-range result use the relevant closest range boundary under the statute, subject to the upward-tax rule.

- Profit split allocates the combined actual profit/loss according to the parties' evidenced functional/asset/risk contributions or other statutory comparable basis; it is not an automatic equal split (art. 96).

For ordinary price and profitability ranges, sort comparable values ascending, keep duplicates and exclude the controlled transaction. For `n` observations, lower rank is `n/4` and upper rank `0.75*n`: at an integer rank average that observation and the next; otherwise take the next integer rank. Index observations starting at one. Profitability uses the transaction year or permitted three preceding years, with weighted averages and working-capital adjustments where required. Special exchange/price-agency and loan rules in art. 92(4)-(4-2) override the ordinary range. Prices inside the range are accepted; below/above use the respective boundary. [Arts. 91(10)-(12), 92(4)-(6)](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0200166).

For qualifying open-ended/demand loans or missing term/currency comparables, art. 92(4-2) uses the specified currency benchmark with a 20% decrease/increase; BYN lending minimum is refinancing rate less 50%, BYN borrowing maximum is refinancing rate plus 20%. Fixed rates use the contract-date benchmark; variable cases use the income/cost-recognition date; repayment requires the statutory actual-term comparison. These are relative multipliers, not percentage-point shifts. Retrieve the actual dated benchmark, rather than quoting a fixed annual rate. [Art. 92(4-2)](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0200166).

**Adjustment.** Calculate the revenue shortfall or excess deductible expense against the lawful boundary; adjust taxable profit/loss only if it does not reduce profit tax. Recalculate cumulative rate and tax under the corporate skill, credit tax already paid, and preserve transaction-level bridge/evidence. A contractual price amendment alone does not discharge a tax adjustment. Domestic TP, profit-tax controlled-debt limits and foreign withholding are separate tests. Apply each relevant rule and avoid deducting more interest merely because the price is arm's length. A treaty corresponding adjustment/MAP requires the specific operative treaty and suspension analysis; unilateral Belarus upward correction does not itself establish foreign relief. See `belarus-cross-border-tax`. [General Code arts. 87-97](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0200166); [Special Code arts. 172, 187-194](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

Calendar-year 2026, BYN. This covers ordinary inbound/outbound individuals and business payments, foreign-company permanent establishments (PEs) and cessation. Identify the legal recipient, tax residence, income source, actual beneficial owner, activity and payment date before selecting the tax. A foreign individual is subject to PIT, not the foreign-company chapter. Belarus-resident individuals and organisations include qualifying foreign-source income; nonresident individuals and non-PE foreign companies are taxed on the respective Belarus-source objects. [General Code arts. 14-17](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0200166); [Special Code arts. 166-169, 188-198](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

These are domestic rates, not treaty rates. A certificate alone does not establish an available treaty article or beneficial ownership. Specific government-debt and other art. 192 relief requires its own facts; there is no universal zero rate for foreign-company interest.

**Residence and individuals.** Under General Code art. 17, count from the day after arrival through departure. Statutory temporary treatment/business absences count; holiday absences count only within the stated aggregate 60-day condition. Prior-year status is provisional for current withholding. Resolve dual residence using the actual operative treaty. Without a resolving treaty, the citizenship/permanent-residence fallback in art. 17(5) applies. Residence permits and nationality alone do not replace this procedure. Residents include foreign receipts under arts. 195-203; the income-tax guide supplies exemptions and deductions. Convert foreign-currency individual receipts at the National Bank rate on actual receipt, with the separate employment and entrepreneur dates in art. 199(11). [General Code art. 17](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0200166); [Special Code arts. 195-214](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

**Foreign-company withholding.** Test the closed Belarus-source income classes in art. 189. Ordinary foreign business turnover is not automatically subject to 15%, and performance abroad does not automatically remove listed consultancy/royalty income. Art. 190(1.3) uses gross income for the residual classes. The specific documented deductions in art. 190(1.1) cover qualifying leasing reimbursement/insurance/financing, specified merchandise operations, real-estate/security/share disposal costs and other listed classes. The agent must possess the documents. For property and company-interest disposals apply the specified historical USD conversions and reconversion at the liability date; do not deduct an unsupported accounting carrying value. Dividends use art. 182(6)'s base via art. 190(1.2). [Arts. 189-190](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

Art. 191 generally recognises the earlier of accounting recognition/completion of the obligation and payment, including noncash settlement. For specified debt interest and contractual sanctions, use the permitted accrual/payment election consistently for the year and mark the return. Convert currency on the applicable liability date under that article. If a contract promises a net amount and requires the payer to bear withholding, gross up the taxable amount before applying the rate, rather than multiplying only the promised net by the rate. [Arts. 190-191](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

**PE profit.** Art. 180 covers a fixed place/branch, a dependent contracting agent, aggregated places performing functions toward a common result, and the service/construction duration tests. Independent ordinary-course agents and exclusively preparatory/auxiliary activities qualify for the stated exceptions only on their actual conduct. Aggregate service days across sites; construction unrelated sites have the separate rule. A PE is recognised from commencement once the duration condition is met. Calculate attributable revenue less evidenced allowable costs and losses using the corporate guide; head-office costs require art. 180(9)-(13)'s allocation, currency and evidence rules, including the prescribed foreign auditor/tax-consultant conclusion unless the local-record exception applies. If profit cannot be evidenced, art. 180(7) provides an agreed allocation or analogous-business assessment, not zero profit. [Arts. 180, 183-186](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

**Foreign-tax credits.** For a Belarus company, art. 187 covers qualifying foreign income tax actually paid/withheld, within Belarus tax on that same income, the tax paid for its income calendar year and the operative treaty amount. Translate at payment date, with art. 187(3)'s certificate-date alternatives. File foreign-authority evidence; art. 187(5) permits specified alternative documents and supplemental contracts/primary records for missing details. Credit normally belongs to the period evidence is filed; evidence filed before the prior annual return deadline can support that annual return or the current period. No unrestricted credit for foreign tax on unrelated income. [Art. 187](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

Resident individual credit under art. 224 is similarly limited to Belarus tax on the qualifying foreign income, subject to the statutory offshore exclusion and any operative treaty. Obtain foreign-authority proof or the permitted declaration/payment evidence. Temporary payer evidence requires the final evidence within the statutory one-year follow-up, otherwise reassessment and interest follow. Entrepreneurs have the separate evidence-filing period, exchange-rate and treaty-cap rules in art. 224(3). [Art. 224(1)-(3)](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

**Offshore levy.** Belarus organisations/entrepreneurs separately test art. 263: payments to offshore-registered recipients or offshore accounts, obligations to those persons, and the specified noncash/assignment transactions. Screen the recipient registration and account jurisdiction against the actual current list in Presidential Decree 353 of 25 May 2006, including subnational entries such as Delaware and Wyoming, rather than treating every US payment identically. [Decree 353](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=P30600353). Apply the exact art. 264 exemptions, including qualifying returned loan principal/interest and specified maritime freight/forwarding conditions, before using the 15% art. 265 transfer/contract base. A withholding-treaty reduction does not by itself remove this separate levy. [Arts. 262-267](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

For a PE, use the quarterly/annual corporate return and payment calendar in the corporate guide. Register/notify the actual activity and preserve local records rather than waiting until day 181. A foreign office/branch registration does not itself prove that every payment is PE-attributable. The agent obtains the Belarus tax office's PE confirmation for the art. 193 exemption by the applicable deadline; otherwise the existence of another PE does not justify withholding nothing. [Arts. 180, 186, 193(4)](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071); [General Code arts. 69-70](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0200166).

On foreign-company/PE cessation, file the final return at least five working days before cessation and settle tax/interest no later than one working day after filing (General Code art. 44(4)). Special Code art. 186(2) uses actual gross profit through cessation. For Belarus-entity liquidation, art. 44(1) requires an initial return within five working days after the liquidation application, tax/interest by the 22nd of the following month, and a final return at least ten working days before the liquidation balance if taxable objects arise during liquidation; the latter settlement is within five working days after that return. Ordinary intervening returns continue unless the paragraph's no-further-object condition applies. The liquidator settles the company's liabilities under art. 44(2). A liquidated branch's return is due by the 20th following the liquidation month and payment by the 22nd of the filing month (art. 44(3)). Use the corporate guide's actual-profit base/rate and separately classify shareholder distributions under arts. 189-190; settlement procedure is not a deemed-disposal exemption. Foreign-entity deregistration under General Code art. 70(4) requires the specified twelve-month interval, clearance of liabilities/penalties and completion of pending audit conditions, followed by the ten-working-day action period; it is not automatic on closing a bank account. This pack does not establish every corporate migration, deemed-disposal or liquidation charge. Do not infer an exemption or zero exit tax from that limit. [General Code arts. 44, 70(4)](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0200166); [Special Code art. 186(2)](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

Late-payment interest under General Tax Code art. 55 is computed separately for each period of constant unpaid tax and National Bank refinancing rate: `unpaid tax × overdue calendar days × annual rate / 360 / 100`. Count from the day after the due date through payment; interest reflected in the audit decision on audit-assessed tax is capped at that assessed tax amount; apply art. 55(3) exclusions and art. 55(4)'s four-decimal interest-rate precision. Use the rate actually in force in each period, not a single assumed 2026 rate. [General Code art. 55](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0200166).

Late agent returns use Administrative Code art. 14.2. Under art. 14.5, the lower withholding-default bracket requires both the amount ceiling (4 basic units for an entrepreneur, 10 for a company) and no more than 5% of the period amount. Fines are 0.4-4 basic units / 2-20 basic units respectively; exceeding either condition invokes 40% of the unpaid amount, minimum 2 / 10 basic units. Responsible-person and intentional-default sanctions are separate. Preserve voluntary-correction/payment facts and assess statutory exceptions before imposing a fine. [Administrative Code arts. 14.2, 14.5](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk2100091).

For each payment, document the recipient country, legal and beneficial owner, income class, treaty's entry/termination status and exact article's suspension status at the relevant date. Council Resolution 164 of 7 March 2024 suspends specified dividend, interest and capital-gain provisions with listed countries for 1 June 2024-31 December 2026; the exact country/article conditions and subsequent changes require checking, not a claim that every treaty with those countries is wholly suspended. The Lithuania treaty terminated from 1 January 2026. Use domestic law where the relevant treaty relief is unavailable. [Resolution 164, para. 2 and annex](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=C22400164); [MNS commencement notice](https://nalog.gov.by/news/23386/); [MNS Lithuania termination](https://nalog.gov.by/news/29303/); [MNS current treaty directory](https://nalog.gov.by/international/double_taxation/).

Art. 194 requires the residence confirmation for the relevant period, with its specified annual/timing exceptions. Beneficial-owner documentation is a separate requirement; the BYN 40,000 aggregate unclaimed-tax documentation exception does not create substantive treaty entitlement. If evidence arrives late, withhold domestically then use the documented refund route. Individuals' residence certificates and refunds use art. 224(4). For outbound corporate claims, obtain a Belarus residence certificate under art. 187(7), naming the foreign country and available income details. Individuals use the prescribed Belarus residence certificate under art. 224(5); foreign residence evidence and treaty refunds remain under art. 224(4). [Arts. 187, 194, 224](https://pravo.by/document/?guid=3871&p0=hk0900071).

VAT place/reverse charge/imports, transfer pricing, controlled debt and social-security coverage are separate tests. A direct-tax business-profit exemption does not settle any of them. This guide supplies the verification procedure, not a comprehensive country-by-country treaty-rate matrix or treaty-specific MAP/APA analysis.
